    12	/// Stream FIFO that does not cut the timing path. When full; pushing data is allowed if in
    13	/// the same cycle data is popped. Creates longer timing paths but can use buffer space more
    14	/// efficiently.
    15	module cc_passthrough_stream_fifo #(
    16	    /// Depth can be arbitrary from 2 to 2**32
    17	    parameter int unsigned Depth       = 32'd8,
    18	    /// Print information when the simulation launches
    19	    parameter bit          PrintInfo   = 1'b0,
    20	    /// If the FIFO is full, allow reading and writing in the same cycle
    21	    parameter bit          SameCycleRW = 1'b1,
    22	    /// Type of the FIFO
    23	    parameter type         data_t      = logic
    24	) (
    25	    /// Clock
    26	    input  logic                 clk_i,
    27	    /// Asynchronous reset active low
    28	    input  logic                 rst_ni,
    29	    /// Synchronous clear active high; clears all sequential logic
    30	    input  logic                 clr_i,
    31	    /// Fifo flush. Compared to clr_i, this only clears internal pointers.
    32	    /// Sufficient for most functional purposes.
    33	    input  logic                 flush_i,
    34	    /// data to push into the FIFO
    35	    input  data_t                data_i,
    36	    /// input data valid
    37	    input  logic                 valid_i,
    38	    /// FIFO is not full
    39	    output logic                 ready_o,
    40	    /// output data
    41	    output data_t                data_o,
    42	    /// FIFO is not empty
    43	    output logic                 valid_o,
    44	    /// pop head from FIFO
    45	    input  logic                 ready_i
    46	);
    47	    /// Bit Width of the read and write pointers
    48	    /// One additional bit to detect overflows
    49	    localparam int unsigned PointerWidth = $clog2(Depth) + 1;
    50	
    51	    // Read and write pointers
    52	    logic [PointerWidth-1:0]  read_ptr_d,  read_ptr_q;
    53	    logic [PointerWidth-1:0] write_ptr_d, write_ptr_q;
    54	
    55	    // Data
    56	    data_t [Depth-1:0] data_d, data_q;
    57	
    58	    // Enable storage
    59	    logic load_data;
    60	
    61	    assign data_o = data_q[read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0]];
    62	
    63	    // Logic
    64	    always_comb begin
    65	        // Default
    66	        load_data   = 1'b0;
    67	        read_ptr_d  = read_ptr_q;
    68	        write_ptr_d = write_ptr_q;
    69	        data_d      = data_q;
    70	
    71	        if (flush_i) begin // Flush
    72	            read_ptr_d  = '0;
    73	            write_ptr_d = '0;
    74	            valid_o     = 1'b0;
    75	            ready_o     = 1'b0;
    76	        end else begin
    77	            // Read
    78	            valid_o = read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1] == write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1]
    79	                ? read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] != write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] : 1'b1;
    80	            if (ready_i && valid_o) begin
    81	                if (read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] == (Depth-1)) begin
    82	                    // On overflow reset pointer to zero and flip imaginary bit
    83	                    read_ptr_d[PointerWidth-2:0] = '0;
    84	                    read_ptr_d[PointerWidth-1]   = !read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1];
    85	                end else begin
    86	                    // Increment counter
    87	                    read_ptr_d = read_ptr_q + 'd1;
    88	                end
    89	            end
    90	
    91	            // Write -> Also able to write if we read in the same cycle
    92	            ready_o     = (read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1] == write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1]
    93	                ? 1'b1 : write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] != read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0])
    94	                || (SameCycleRW && ready_i && valid_o);
    95	
    96	            if (valid_i && ready_o) begin
    97	                load_data = 1'b1;
    98	                data_d[write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0]] = data_i;
    99	
   100	                if (write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] == (Depth-1)) begin
   101	                    // On overflow reset pointer to zero and flip imaginary bit
   102	                    write_ptr_d[PointerWidth-2:0] = '0;
   103	                    write_ptr_d[PointerWidth-1]   = !write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1];
   104	                end else begin
   105	                    // Increment pointer
   106	                    write_ptr_d = write_ptr_q + 'd1;
   107	                end
   108	            end
   109	        end
   110	    end
   111	
   112	    // Flip Flops
   113	    `FFARNC( read_ptr_q,  read_ptr_d, clr_i, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   114	    `FFARNC(write_ptr_q, write_ptr_d, clr_i, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   115	
   116	    `FFLARNC(data_q, data_d, load_data, clr_i, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   117	
   118	endmodule

    16	module cc_fifo #(
    17	    parameter bit          FallThrough = 1'b0, // fifo is in fall-through mode
    18	    parameter int unsigned DataWidth   = 32,   // default data width if the fifo is of type logic
    19	    parameter int unsigned Depth       = 8,    // depth can be arbitrary from 0 to 2**32
    20	    parameter type         data_t      = logic [DataWidth-1:0],
    21	    // DO NOT OVERWRITE THIS PARAMETER
    22	    localparam int unsigned UsageWidth = cc_pkg::cnt_width(Depth)
    23	)(
    24	    input  logic  clk_i,   // Clock
    25	    input  logic  rst_ni,  // Asynchronous reset active low
    26	    input  logic  clr_i,   // Synchronous clear active high; clears internal pointers *and*
    27	                           // memories.
    28	    input  logic  flush_i, // Flush the queue; compared to clr_i this only clears internal pointers.
    29	                           // Sufficient for most functional purposes.
    30	    // Status flags
    31	    output logic  full_o,  // Queue is full
    32	    output logic  empty_o, // Queue is empty
    33	    output logic  [UsageWidth-1:0] usage_o,  // Fill pointer
    34	    // As long as the queue is not full we can push new data
    35	    input  data_t data_i,  // Data to push into the queue
    36	    input  logic  push_i,  // Data is valid and can be pushed to the queue
    37	    // As long as the queue is not empty we can pop new elements
    38	    output data_t data_o,  // Output data
    39	    input  logic  pop_i    // Pop head from queue
    40	);
    41	    // local parameter
    42	    // FIFO depth - handle the case of pass-through, synthesizer will do constant propagation
    43	    localparam int unsigned FifoDepth = (Depth > 0) ? Depth : 1;
    44	    localparam int unsigned PtrWidth = cc_pkg::idx_width(Depth);
    45	    // clock gating control
    46	    logic gate_clock;
    47	    // pointer to the read and write section of the queue
    48	    logic [PtrWidth-1:0] read_pointer_n, read_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, write_pointer_q;
    49	    // keep a counter to keep track of the current queue status
    50	    // this integer will be truncated by the synthesis tool
    51	    logic [UsageWidth-1:0] status_cnt_n, status_cnt_q;
    52	    // actual memory
    53	    data_t [FifoDepth - 1:0] mem_n, mem_q;
    54	
    55	    assign usage_o = status_cnt_q;
    56	
    57	    if (Depth == 0) begin : gen_pass_through
    58	        assign empty_o     = ~push_i;
    59	        assign full_o      = ~pop_i;
    60	    end else begin : gen_fifo
    61	        assign full_o       = (status_cnt_q == FifoDepth[UsageWidth-1:0]);
    62	        assign empty_o      = (status_cnt_q == 0) & ~(FallThrough & push_i);
    63	    end
    64	    // status flags
    65	
    66	    // read and write queue logic
    67	    always_comb begin : read_write_comb
    68	        // default assignment
    69	        read_pointer_n  = read_pointer_q;
    70	        write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
    71	        status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q;
    72	        data_o          = (Depth == 0) ? data_i : mem_q[read_pointer_q];
    73	        mem_n           = mem_q;
    74	        gate_clock      = 1'b1;
    75	
    76	        // push a new element to the queue
    77	        if (push_i && ~full_o) begin
    78	            // push the data onto the queue
    79	            mem_n[write_pointer_q] = data_i;
    80	            // un-gate the clock, we want to write something
    81	            gate_clock = 1'b0;
    82	            // increment the write counter
    83	            // this is dead code when Depth is a power of two
    84	            if (write_pointer_q == FifoDepth[PtrWidth-1:0] - 1)
    85	                write_pointer_n = '0;
    86	            else
    87	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q + 1;
    88	            // increment the overall counter
    89	            status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q + 1;
    90	        end
    91
